La CEUS mostra la vascolarizzazione in t:
CEUS shows vascularity in real time. A part that does not enhance in any phase has no flow: it is necrosis, fluid, blood or pus.
A pyogenic abscess on CEUS typically has a rim and often internal septa that enhance in the arterial phase, a center that never enhances and sometimes hyperemia of the surrounding parenchyma; in the late phases the rim may lose contrast. On B-mode, in the early stages, it may be only an ill-defined hypoechoic area, as here.
The main differential diagnosis is tumors with central necrosis (metastases, cholangiocarcinoma): the solid rim of a tumor loses contrast early and markedly (LR-M category in patients at risk). CEUS alone is not always enough: the clinical picture (fever, leukocytosis, CRP, biliary or intestinal sources) and aspiration decide, and aspiration is also therapeutic.
